dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a small, flat-bottomed 826 ppm dip every 13.9 days that repeats consistently in 4 transits on a star with no close neighbours that could mimic it. No odd-even difference or secondary eclipse points to a binary, and depth is steady, favouring a 2.3 Earth-radius planet despite a low SNR and no centroid detection. The period is near the star’s 8.5-day rotation with strong spot variability, and the duration looks long, so additional photometry and radial velocities are needed to confirm the planet and rule out activity.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed transit (negative V significance) positively favours a planet over a grazing binary.
Small-planet size from undiluted depth 840.2 ppm favors planet over stellar companion.
Depth steady between sectors (686 ppm vs 848 ppm within errors) and sector_depths_by_source steady; no sector-dependent change.
4 individual transits consistent (chi2 5.96 dof3), no outliers driving signal; top 3 share 0.925 but SNR 10.44 remains low.
No star within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can plausibly cause the 825.9 ppm dip with an eclipse <=25%, against a neighbour EB.
Odd/even not significant and secondary.snr 1.702 with best_brightening_snr 4.037 well below threshold; no binary signature.
